newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wine sector expects grape shortfall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wine sector expects grape shortfall.

text.p: Australian winemakers could expect a shortfall in the amount of grapes available to meet their needs over the next three years, according to a report released on Friday.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) report combined estimates of the 1995/96 harvest with projections of wine grape production for the three years to 1998/99 on a varietal and regional basis.
"Over the next three years, winemakers can expect wine grape production to be marginally below their preferred intake," ABARE executive director Brian Fisher said in a statement.
Fisher said the report found that between 1996/97 and 1998/99, winemakers planned to increase their wine grape intake by about 181,000 tonnes.
"Although production is expected to increase over this period, there is projected to be a 27,000 tonne shortfall relative to winemakers' planned intake in 1998/99," he said.
The report found that premium wine grapes were expected to make up the major portion of planned intake growth, while a decline in intake was planned for most non-premium and multipurpose grapes.
"Winemakers had indicated that the biggest increases in the tonnages they plan to crush by 1998/99 would be for the chardonnay, semillon, shiraz and cabernet sauvignon varieties," Fisher said.
He said premium wine grape varieties were forecast to account for almost 97 percent of the increase in wine grape production between 1996/97 and 1998/99.
